product_versions: Azure CLI with az account get-access-token --scope (for example 2.91.0)
can_disable_login_prompt_note: The script never prompts. Sign-in happens only through az login.

telemetry_controls.effect: Keeps the Azure CLI sign-in state in a separate folder.

auth.method: az account get-access-token --scope api://<apim-app-id>/.default; prints the raw JWT to stdout
auth.notes: Guards: stdout filter keeps only the JWT-shaped line; audience check against $ExpectedAud; lifetime check of 60 seconds. Exit 0 prints the JWT; exit 1 prints one stderr line (az failed, no JWT, wrong audience, token expires in N s). Azure CLI client ID 04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46 must be pre-authorized on the app registration or consented by an administrator. Latency: about 0.6 s for az to fail when not signed in (helper reports in about 0.8 s); token fetch time on a real tenant is not established.

config_snippets.content:
# Prints ONLY the raw JWT to stdout; on any problem prints a one-line reason to stderr and exits 1.
# Failing fast matters: both Claude Code and Codex retry hard on a bad token.
$Scope       = 'api://<apim-app-id>/.default'
$ExpectedAud = @('api://<apim-app-id>', '<apim-app-client-id>')   # accept both token forms
$MinLifeSecs = 60

$lines = & az account get-access-token --scope $Scope --query accessToken -o tsv 2>$null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine("get-apim-token: az failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE). Run: az login"); exit 1 }

# Tolerate banners/warnings on stdout: keep only the line that looks like a JWT.
$jwt = $lines | ForEach-Object { "$_".Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ -match '^eyJ[\w-]+\.[\w-]+\.[\w-]+$' } | Select-Object -Last 1
if (-not $jwt) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine('get-apim-token: az output contained no JWT'); exit 1 }

# Sanity-check the claims so a wrong audience or nearly-expired token fails here, not as an endless 401 loop.
$p = $jwt.Split('.')[1].Replace('-', '+').Replace('_', '/')
while ($p.Length % 4) { $p += '=' }
$claims = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([Convert]::FromBase64String($p)) | ConvertFrom-Json
$now = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
if ($ExpectedAud -notcontains $claims.aud) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine("get-apim-token: token aud is '$($claims.aud)', expected '$($ExpectedAud -join "' or '")'"); exit 1 }
if ($claims.exp - $now -lt $MinLifeSecs) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine("get-apim-token: token expires in $($claims.exp - $now)s"); exit 1 }

[Console]::Out.Write($jwt)

hosts_default: Microsoft Entra sign-in and token endpoints (only when a new token is needed)
hosts_after_config: Microsoft Entra sign-in and token endpoints (only when a new token is needed)
limits: GUI-launched hosts may lack az on PATH; use the full path to az.cmd.
Tokens last as set by the tenant (typically 60 to 90 minutes); keep caller cache or refresh intervals below it.
Conditional Access sign-in frequency decides when az login is needed again.
v1 and v2 tokens can carry different aud values; set $ExpectedAud from a real token.
